comment: Single place to swap the on-device model. Everything here is data: the app never hard-codes a model name, URL or checksum. After changing model.* update sha256 with tools/ai/model_checksum.py and bump model.version so devices re-download.

lowMemory.comment: Applied automatically on a device that passes minRamMB but is under recommendedRamMB - every phone with 4 GB of memory or less, which is most of them. The same model file runs with a shorter context and a shorter answer so it fits the memory the OS leaves the app.

device.comment: A device below minRamMB never loads the LLM. The assistant then runs the same pipeline with the model disabled and answers through grounded smart search plus a ready-made information card. The model file is under 500 MB, so a 3 GB phone (iPhone X, XR, SE 2, most budget Androids) can hold it, and minRamMB sits just above what a 2 GB device reports because the OS kills the app while that model loads. recommendedRamMB is where the full context size is used, and it is set above 4 GB on purpose: a 4 GB phone reports about 3.7-4.0 GB, so the whole 4 GB class now runs the lean profile instead of the 2048-token window, because the model file plus the app's own copy of the medicine index is what pushes a 4 GB device past what the OS leaves it. Only devices reporting more than 4 GB get the full window.
device.minFreeRamMBComment: minFreeRamMBAtLoad refuses a load when the OS reports less free memory than that. On Android the reported figure is MemAvailable, and a healthy 4 GB phone routinely sits between 350 and 600 MB because the OS keeps spare RAM as reclaimable cache, so a lean device uses lowMemoryMinFreeRamMBAtLoad instead of being refused on a phone that can load the shorter profile. The runtime on Apple reports half of total RAM as free, so this gate only bites on Android. The guard against over-committing stays the memory-pressure unload below, which releases the model without losing the download.

paths.comment: App-private storage only. iOS/macOS: Application Support/Dawaya/models. Android: getNoBackupFilesDir or filesDir. Windows: %LOCALAPPDATA%\Dawaya\models.

web.comment: The web/PWA runtime: llama.cpp compiled to WebAssembly (wllama, MIT), vendored untouched so the browser build has no CDN and no account. The pinned hashes are enforced by scripts/privacy-check.py; keep them and ai/vendor/wllama/README.txt in sync when upgrading. Threads need cross-origin isolation; without it the model still runs single-threaded. The Safari build (compat) is local too, never the jsDelivr fallback.
